scope: Developer fixed reference-tool admission seam in the unchanged base conversation/history lifecycle; fake providers plus actual stdio retrieval under explicitly synthetic demo context.
checks: Missing/duplicate/writable reference-tool admission refuses before provider construction or durable turn creation.
Only the two fixed reference names are added per turn. Strict local request validation, current definition/annotation rechecks and existing serialized 64-KiB chat-evidence limits apply.
Completion uses the existing durable history lifecycle/provider close; cancellation retains the original cancellation path and revokes the task-local grant.
Inherited child contexts are revoked after completion; a deliberately late child cannot issue a new reference read. Two concurrent chats keep separate grants/providers/histories.
Actual stdio search/get returns original grid and no-construction/no-execution qualifiers through durable tool evidence, with no production global allowlist mutation.

fixture_context.session_id: New fixture UUID generated at test time
fixture_context.captured_at: Current fixture timestamp, not a native observation

limits: Fake providers drive chosen tool requests and final text. No DeepSeek/other model schema compatibility, real reasoning/advice quality, inference, native game/UI or paired player release is established.
The synthetic demo context remains explicitly unverified; a generated UUID/current test timestamp do not establish a live world. Existing parent session/freshness rules are not bypassed.

Task grants and definition rechecks are finite cooperative async checks, not general malicious-provider/remote-server or arbitrary task security acceptance. Revocation does not undo an already dispatched external request.
The production coordinator/CLI does not instantiate this subclass. Published nineteen-tool admission, normal histories, production Java/Python payload and tested bundles remain unchanged.

Native catalog and original geometry retain their earlier exact scopes. No construction legality, actual pathfinding, optimality, cost/capacity, gameplay action or third-party layout/rights validation follows.
